content:
Japan-Vietnam relations have entered a new phase. Since the November 2023 upgrade to a “Comprehensive Strategic Partnership for Peace and Prosperity in Asia and the World,” the two governments have steadily expanded cooperation across economic security, the green transition, advanced technology, maritime and security cooperation, and development. The question now is not how much more can be added to the bilateral agenda, but whether the two countries can turn an increasingly ambitious partnership into tangible economic and strategic results.
This evolving relationship reflects two distinct strategic calculations. They are complementary, but not identical. For Japan, Vietnam is becoming increasingly important to economic security, supply chain diversification, and resilience, particularly in energy and critical minerals. In May 2026, the two governments identified economic security as a new priority for bilateral relations, focusing on energy, critical minerals, AI, semiconductors, and space. For Vietnam, the emphasis remains on independence, self-reliance, diversification, and multilateralization in its external relations. The partnership will work best when it expands both countries’ strategic options rather than forcing alignment into an exclusive framework.
Economic Security Without Strategic Polarization
Energy security offers the clearest test of this new phase of partnership amid continued geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East. Support for the Nghi Son refinery shows how bilateral cooperation can serve both countries’ interests. At their May 2026 summit, Japan and Vietnam agreed to proceed with support from NEXI, Japan’s official export credit agency, for crude oil procurement for Nghi Son. It will be the first project under POWERR Asia, a broader partnership designed to maintain crude oil and petroleum production and key supply chains.
On rare earths and other critical minerals, Japan sees Vietnam as an important partner in diversifying supply chains and reducing dependence on China. But Vietnam remains closely tied to China, which produces over 90 percent of the world’s refined rare earths and almost all high-performance magnets. Vietnam still lacks independent separation and refining capacity. As its electronics and EV industries expand, this dependence may deepen. Against this backdrop, the May summit treated critical minerals cooperation more cautiously, emphasizing continued discussions rather than announcing concrete projects.
For Vietnam, mineral resources alone do not automatically translate into an autonomous supply chain. Developing domestic processing, technological capability, and downstream industries will take time. Economic resilience is not the same as economic decoupling from China. Given these constraints, the most tangible near-term progress will likely come in energy security, while critical minerals cooperation can be expected to advance more gradually and selectively.
Vietnam’s foreign policy centers on independence and self-reliance, coupled with a diversified and multilateral external posture. Japan’s most valuable contribution may therefore be to broaden Vietnam’s economic and technological options rather than frame the relationship as a choice between strategic partners. Japan has relatively little to gain from presenting its engagement as an effort to draw Vietnam away from China. Its greater contribution lies in giving Vietnam a wider range of economic and technological options.
Advanced Technology as the New Growth Engine
Looking further ahead, some of the greatest opportunities lie at the intersection of advanced technology, digitalization, the green transition, semiconductors, and human capital. The challenge is to pursue them as part of a wider economic and industrial ecosystem rather than as separate initiatives.
Some foundations are already in place. Japan and Vietnam are establishing cooperation channels through the Asia Zero Emission Community (AZEC), while the Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM) provides a bilateral framework for decarbonization technologies and infrastructure. Cooperation is also extending into science and technology, semiconductors, AI, energy, critical minerals, and agriculture. Specific areas include semiconductor R&D and education, AI and human resource development, satellite data, digital transformation, and energy cooperation.
The larger strategic prize is not any single investment but a durable ecosystem connecting skills, research and development, manufacturing, supply chains, and ultimately markets across the two economies. Japan can contribute capital, technology, an established industrial base, and institutional know-how, while Vietnam offers an expanding production base and a growing pool of human resources. A long-term road map, with carefully chosen flagship projects at its heart, could turn these complementary strengths into industrial upgrading and a more substantial economic relationship.
The Implementation Challenge
The challenge is not simply to raise ambition but to create the conditions for that ambition to be realized. Persistent concerns among Japanese businesses make regulatory predictability, administrative efficiency, access to financing, and appropriate risk-sharing essential to the bilateral economic agenda. Japan’s focus at the May 2026 summit on the investment and economic cooperation environment is a clear example. Ultimately, strategic cooperation will be credible only if it produces projects that are economically viable and sustainable without indefinite government support.
The Japan-Vietnam Joint Initiative is a key institutional underpinning. Established in 2003 to support improvements in Vietnam’s investment climate and institutional framework, it reflects Japan’s long-standing commitment to addressing practical impediments to the bilateral relationship. But the context has changed considerably. Vietnam has developed significantly in its capabilities and in the range of partners it can now engage with. History gives Japan credibility in Vietnam, but it does not guarantee future relevance. Japan must demonstrate the specific value a deeper relationship can bring.
Both sides therefore need to further substantiate the partnership. Vietnam can continue working to create a more transparent and predictable investment climate, while Japan can go beyond identifying institutional impediments to put forward a more compelling economic case.
A disciplined approach to risk is just as important. Government support should address risks the market cannot efficiently bear, not shield private investors from ordinary commercial risk. Clear allocation of risk between government and business should be central to public-private collaboration. An arm’s-length relationship upholds the investor’s autonomy and ownership, rather than subordinating their interests to the government’s geopolitical objectives.
An Autonomous Partnership for Regional Stability
The same logic applies to regional and security cooperation. Vietnam has become an increasingly important partner in Japan’s Indo-Pacific diplomacy under the updated Free and Open Indo-Pacific (FOIP). Vietnam’s commitment to strategic autonomy is not an obstacle to deeper cooperation with Japan. It is precisely what makes a non-exclusive partnership politically sustainable.
There is ample scope for deeper cooperation on the maritime order, climate resilience, energy security, and technological resilience in ways that serve both countries’ interests while respecting Vietnam’s diplomatic independence. This aligns with the principles set out in the 2023 Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, particularly international law, sovereignty, independence, peace, and shared prosperity.
The relationship therefore goes well beyond bilateral interests. Japan and Vietnam can show that a meaningful strategic relationship is possible without being exclusive. ASEAN-centric institutions, APEC, and other international fora provide mechanisms through which this can contribute to regional stability and cooperation.
The timing of General Secretary and State President To Lam’s visit from November 8 to November 11 is very deliberate. With a summit coming just before APEC and the ASEAN-related meetings, both countries can highlight their bilateral cooperation within broader regional discussions on supply chains, energy transition, and nontraditional security.
The first phase of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership was about building the architecture of cooperation. The next is about implementation. Japan’s technology, finance, capacity to develop human capital, and ability to share appropriate risk can be brought together to support Vietnam’s development priorities. At the same time, a more transparent and predictable investment climate in Vietnam will be essential for turning strategic intent into actual projects.
The next phase of Japan-Vietnam relations should therefore be judged less by the number of agreements signed than by whether the partnership produces bankable projects, stronger capabilities, and greater economic resilience. Japan does not need Vietnam to choose between strategic partners, and Vietnam does not need Japan simply to add another diplomatic framework. What both need is a partnership that expands their room for maneuvering while delivering tangible economic value.
Following Lam’s visit to Japan next week, the next test will be whether the two governments can translate another round of high-level diplomacy into tangible results and measurable progress.
summary: The question now is whether the two countries can turn their increasingly ambitious partnership into tangible economic and strategic results.
summary_th: คำถามก็คือว่าทั้งสองประเทศสามารถเปลี่ยนความร่วมมือที่ทะเยอทะยานมากขึ้นให้กลายเป็นผลลัพธ์ทางเศรษฐกิจและยุทธศาสตร์ที่จับต้องได้หรือไม่

content:
‘โบว์ เมลดา’ แฮปปี้ปีทอง รับงานแน่นจนไม่มีเวลาพัก ปัดโกยเงินสร้างเรือนหอ ลั่นรอ ‘อาเล็ก’ คุกเข่าสวมแหวนก่อน
เรียกว่าคิวงานแน่นจนแทบไม่มีเวลาพัก สำหรับนางเอกสาว โบว์ เมลดา ที่ปีนี้มีทั้งงานแสดง ภาพยนตร์ และงานอื่นๆ เข้ามารัวๆ ล่าสุดโบว์ มาร่วมให้สัมภาษณ์ภาพยนตร์คอเมดี้ฟอร์มยักษ์จาก Netflix เรื่อง แก๊งโอเวอร์ ณ โรงภาพยนตร์ พารากอน ซีนีเพล็กซ์ ชั้น 5 ศูนย์การค้าสยามพารากอน เจ้าตัวก็ยอมรับเป็นคนชอบทำงาน ไม่อยากปฏิเสธโอกาสที่ผู้ใหญ่หยิบยื่นให้ แม้เคยขอหยุดสัปดาห์ละ 2 วันเพื่อรีโนเวตตัวเอง แต่สุดท้ายก็ต้องรับงานยาวจนแทบไม่มีวันหยุด พร้อมอัพเดตความคืบหน้าสร้างบ้านที่เจอปัญหาจุกจิกจนปวดหัว
ปีนี้งานโบว์เยอะมาก ทั้งงานแสดง ภาพยนตร์ และงานต่างๆ เข้ามาติดๆ กันเลย? เรียกว่าเป็นปีทองของเราเลย?
“เราชอบทำงาน ก็เลยไม่ค่อยได้ปฏิเสธงานสักเท่าไหร่ ถ้าเป็นไปได้ก็ไม่อยากปฏิเสธ เพราะผู้ใหญ่อุตส่าห์ให้โอกาสเรา แล้วถ้าทำไหวก็จะทำ ถ้าจังหวะมันไม่ได้ซ้อนอะไรกันเยอะก็ยินดีรับค่ะ”
แสดงว่าโบว์ไม่ได้เลือกบทมากขนาดนั้น ไม่เม็ด?
“ไม่เม็ดๆ เม็ดเหรอ? หลายเม็ดเหมือนกันนะ”
ปกติเวลารับงานแสดงต้องดูอะไร บทบาทต้องไม่ซ้ำกันไหม?
“ก็ไม่นะคะ เพราะทุกคาแรกเตอร์มันต่างกันอยู่แล้ว อยู่ที่ว่าเราจะเล่นยังไงให้ต่างจากเดิม ทั้งน้ำเสียง ท่าทาง เสื้อผ้า หน้าผม หรืออะไรที่มันต่างกันทั้งหมดอยู่แล้ว ถามว่าเลือกไหมก็ไม่ได้เลือกขนาดนั้น รับหมด (ถ้าใครยื่นบทมาแล้วบทไม่ติดอะไร เราก็เล่นเลย?) ใช่ บทไม่ติด เวลาไม่ติด เราก็ยินดีทำงาน (ก็เลยเป็นสาเหตุที่ทำให้เรามีหนังเยอะ มีงานแสดงเยอะ?) ใช่”
ปีนี้คิวยังเหลืออยู่ไหม?
“เป็นคำถามที่ถามตัวเองทุกวันเหมือนกันว่า ฉันจะได้ไปทำอะไรที่ตัวเองอยากทำบ้างไหม ไอ้งานก็อยากทำ แต่บางทีก็ต้องหาเวลาไปเติม ไปบำรุงผม บำรุงผิว เข้าคลินิกบ้าง ต้องเจอบ้าง (แล้วมีไหม?) น้อยค่ะ”
ช่วงหยุดยาว เราหยุดกี่วัน?
“เขามีวันหยุดกันด้วยเหรอ (วันหยุดเสาร์-อาทิตย์รู้จักไหม?) อุ้ย เคยได้ยินตั้งแต่เด็กๆ (พอโตมาปุ๊บไม่เคยได้ยินแล้ว?) โตมาเขายังมีกันอยู่เหรอคะ (วันนี้วันอะไร รู้ไหมโบว์?) วันที่ 4 (แต่ไม่จำแล้วว่าวันจันทร์ อังคาร พุธ ไม่รู้เรื่อง?) ไม่รู้”
เราอยากขอผู้จัดส่วนตัวไหมว่า ถ้าอย่างนั้นขอวันหยุดหน่อยได้ไหม?
“เคยขอเขาว่าอาทิตย์หนึ่งเราสามารถหยุดได้สัก 2 วันไหม เพื่อที่จะได้มีเวลารีโนเวตตัวเองบ้าง เพราะบางทีเราไปโลเกชันต่างๆ เราเป็นคนที่ค่อนข้างผิวเซ้นส์ซิทีฟมาก ก็อยากไปเติมอะไรที่ช่วยให้ผิวแข็งแรงขึ้น โดนแดดนิดหน่อยโบว์ก็ผื่นขึ้นแล้ว เพราะแต่ละโลเกชันหรือแม้แต่ในโรงหนัง หรืออะไรก็ตามฝุ่นมันเยอะอยู่แล้ว แล้วถ้าเราพักผ่อนน้อย ภูมิคุ้มกันก็จะตก เราก็เลยอยากถามว่าสามารถไหมแบบหยุดอาทิตย์ละ 2 วัน เคยทำได้อยู่หนึ่งอาทิตย์ หลังจากนั้นก็พี่โบว์มีงานนี้เข้ามา อ้าว งานดี ก็รับ หลังจากนั้นก็รับยาวเลย ไม่มีวันหยุดเลย”
เอาเงินไปทำอะไรบ้าง เคยคิดไหม?
“ไม่รู้เหมือนกันค่ะ ตอนนี้ยังไม่เห็นตัวเงิน กำลังค่อยๆ ทำงาน แล้วค่อยไปดูใหม่อีกทีในตอนที่ได้พัก (เราได้ความภูมิใจว่าเราเก็บหอมรอมริบ?) แต่บางงานก็ไม่ได้เงินก็มี เราก็ช่วยๆ กัน เป็นงานช่วย
จริงไหมที่ว่าทำงานหนักถึงขั้นทรุดตัวลงไปร้องไห้ตอนขึ้นรถหลังจากงานเสร็จ?
“พี่ดูเรื่องอะไร ไม่ใช่แก๊งโอเวอร์นะ ”
ถามไปก่อนเผื่อได้พาดหัวเด็ดๆ อารมณ์แบบไม่ไหวแล้ว อยากทรุดตัวร้องไห้ มีไหม ฉันทำอะไรอยู่เนี่ย ทำไมฉันเหนื่อยจังเลย?
“หรือว่ามีแต่ไม่รู้ตัววะ (มีไหม?) ไม่มีค่ะ ไม่เคยเป็น ชอบทำงาน อยากเจอพี่ๆ ทุกวันเลย”
หรือว่าเรามองว่าโอกาสมันต้องโกยไว้ก่อน?
“ถ้าเป็นพี่ๆ หลายคนก็บอกว่าถ้ามีโอกาสก็โกยไว้ก็ดี ก็ดีแล้วที่มีงานทำ”
ตอนนี้ขาขึ้นของเราเลยหรือเปล่า?
“ไม่ค่อยขึ้นนะคะ มันก็เรื่อยๆ เป็นฟีลเรื่อยๆ โบว์จะไม่ได้เป็นฟีลแบบตู้ม!!อย่างนั้น แต่จะเป็นแบบค่อยๆ เป็นค่อยๆ ไป อยู่ไปเรื่อยๆ แฮปปี้อะไรแบบนี้มากกว่า”
แต่ไม่เกี่ยวกับการเก็บเงินไปสร้างบ้าน สร้างเรือนหออะไรแบบนี้?
“เรือนหออาจจะยัง เขายังไม่ได้ขอ”
มีออกแบบไว้บ้างหรือยัง เพราะเขาบอกว่าให้เราร่วมออกแบบด้วย?
“ยังค่ะยัง รอให้เขาสวมแหวนก่อน รอให้เขาคุกเข่าก่อน เดี๋ยวคิดไปคิดมา เอ้า! แบบมี แต่อาจจะไม่ใช่บ้านเราอะไรอย่างนี้ งานเข้า รอก่อนนะคะ”
แต่เรื่องนี้เราก็สามารถเรื่อยๆ ไปก่อน ไม่ได้รีบ?
“ใช่ ไม่รีบค่ะ”
แล้วคุณอาเล็กเขารีบไหม?
“เขาก็แล้วแต่หนูนะ เขารู้ว่าเราชอบทำงาน แล้วถ้ามันจะเกิดขึ้น ก็คงเป็นเวลาที่เหมาะสม ไม่รู้อ่ะ ไม่กล้าคอนเฟิร์มว่าจะเกิดขึ้นเมื่อไหร่ เพราะเราไม่ใช่คนขอ เขาขอ”
ทำไมเราไม่ลองเปลี่ยนเป็นฝ่ายขอเขาเอง?
“เคยคิดจะขอแล้ว แต่ไม่ได้ (ทำไม?) ขนาดขอตังค์ยังไม่ให้เลย ก็เลยเดี๋ยวค่อยว่ากัน ไปเรื่อยปะ”
หรือต้องรอบ้านเสร็จก่อนไหม?
“คือตอนนี้ของตัวบ้านโบว์เองก็ปัญหาเยอะแยะไปหมด ก็เลยค่อยว่ากันแล้วกันนะเรื่องคุกเข่า เอาให้บ้านนี่จบก่อน เดี๋ยวค่อยว่ากัน เพราะว่า ปวดหัวอยู่เหมือนกัน”
เป็นไงบ้างบ้านเราที่บอกว่าเจอปัญหาเยอะ?
“พูดได้เหรอคะ (พูดได้ เราไม่พาดพิงชื่อใครไง?) มันก็มีปัญหาเล็กๆ น้อยๆ ล่ะค่ะในการทำบ้าน เป็นเรื่องปัญหาของคนในการพูดคุยติดต่อสื่อสารกัน บางครั้งมันก็จะมีความไม่ตรงตามประเด็น เหมือนเราคุยกันแบบนี้ สเปกบ้านทุกอย่างก็ดีหมด แค่เรื่องการติดต่อว่าไอ้นี้จะต้องอย่างนั้น อย่างนี้”
เราเป็นคนที่ต้องคุยเองทั้งหมด หรือมีเอเจนซี่?
“ไม่มีเอเจนซี่เลย ตัวบ้านยังไม่ได้เริ่มตกแต่งอะไรเลย แต่ตั้งแต่โครงสร้างบ้าน ตั้งแต่เริ่มสร้างบ้าน เริ่มอะไรเลยของหมู่บ้าน ก็มีปัญหาเล็กๆ น้อยๆ ประมาณนึง ที่แบบ…มาทำไมวะ อะไรคุณพี่ ทำไมต้องเร่งอะไรขนาดนั้น นี่ยังไม่ได้เข้าไปดูบ้านเลย
แล้วตัวโบว์ได้เข้าไปดูหน้างานบ้างไหม?
“มีเข้าไปบ้างค่ะ แต่จริงๆ ตอนนี้ต้องหาวันเข้าไปดู ก็พอจะขอวันเขาดูได้บ้าง”
ตอนนี้เคลียร์กันลงตัวหรือยัง ทั้งเรื่องการแก้ไขและความรับผิดชอบต่างๆ?
“ก็พยายามให้มันลงตัวค่ะ เพราะถ้าไม่ลงตัว จะมีคนทุบให้อยู่แล้ว”
แต่ตัวเราไม่กังวลใจใช่ไหม?
“ก็กังวลค่ะ แต่งบอาจจะไม่บานปลาย เพราะมีสปอนเซอร์มาช่วยเหลือเราเยอะมาก อยากจะให้ตรงนี้เรา ให้ความกรุณาทำตรงนี้ให้ทั้งหมด คือคนช่วยเราเยอะ แต่มันมีปัญหาตรงก่อนจะรับโอนบ้านนี่แหละ ทั้งเรื่องข้อบกพร่องต่างๆ มันหลากหลาย?
ปวดหัวอยู่แล้ว การทำบ้านเนอะ?
“ใช่ การทำบ้านก็เป็นเรื่องปกติที่ต้องเจอหลากหลายเรื่องราว หลากหลายผู้คน”
ฤกษ์เข้าอยู่ยังเหมือนเดิมไหม?
“เลิกแล้วค่ะ แต่ตอนนี้ไม่ตีกับนิติบุคคลในหมู่บ้านก็บุญละ พยายามจะดีลกับเขาให้ดีที่สุด แล้วเขาก็พยายามจะดูแลเราให้ดีที่สุด ก็โอเค เชื่อมั่นเขา”
summary: ‘โบว์ เมลดา’ แฮปปี้ปีทอง รับงานแน่นจนไม่มีเ […]

Traffic gridlock at Malaysia-Singapore causeway after Woodlands blackout
Although all Malaysian customs counters were open, the jam lasted for many hours due to a build-up of vehicles from Singapore
Although all counters were operating at optimum level at the Bangunan Sultan Iskandar Customs, Immigration and Quarantine complex in the southern state of Johor, the jam lasted for many hours due to a build-up of vehicles from the Singapore side.
It is learnt that the issue started at about noon on the Singapore side. A Malaysian home ministry official said the situation was worsened by a truck heading to Singapore experiencing mechanical failure.

A mother and daughter are dead in a suspected grizzly bear attack near Bella Coola, British Columbia, devastating their family, according to the victims' relatives and B.C. Conservation Officer Service.
Family members identified the victims as Jennifer Balcarras and her 20-year-old daughter, Selah Reed.
The victims were first reported missing on Nov. 1, after they failed to return from what was expected to be a short afternoon walk.
"The way it starts is a few hours of not hearing from them," said Josh Balcarras, Balcarras' brother, in an interview with CBS News Canadian partner CBC News. "That turns into a day, and then a night … then a second night comes and it becomes a real thing."
Balcarras' body was discovered in the Snooka West Trail area on Monday afternoon. Reed's remains were found on Tuesday. Agencies including the Royal Canadian Mounted Police and local search and rescue authorities took part in the investigation, said Jeff Tyre, an inspector with the B.C. Conservation Officer Service. Tyre announced the discovery of the two sets of the remains on social media.
"Our thoughts are with the family of the victims during this tragic time. We are in contact with the family to offer any support we can as we continue to investigate this incident," Tyre said in one video.
Tyre said it is not clear how many bears were involved. Efforts to locate and capture any involved animals are underway, he said. Captured bears will be assessed. If it is determined to have been involved in the attack, it will be "dispatched in accordance with provincial human-wildlife conflict response guidelines to protect public safety," Tyre said. Tyre urged the public to avoid the Snooka West Trail area while this work is underway.
"Two peas in a pod"
Balcarras and Reed were "two peas in a pod" who "got along really, really well" and shared many hobbies, Josh Balcarras told CBC.
"When Jenny hiked, Selah was right there beside her," Josh Balcarras told CBC.
The family has started a GoFundMe to cover funeral costs. Balcarras had recently moved to Bella Coola to pursue a new career and start a fresh chapter in her life, according to the fundraiser. Because of the move, she did not have savings, her family wrote. Balcarras leaves behind three young adult children and a grandchild.
Reed had "her whole life ahead of her," the family wrote, and "was only beginning her journey into adulthood."
Bear attacks in British Columbia
There are between 10,000 and 13,000 grizzly bears estimated to live in British Columbia, according to the province's Ministry of Environment, Lands and Parks. The species is classified as vulnerable. Conflicts between grizzly bears and humans are considered "relatively rare," the ministry said, unless the animals are startled or protecting their cubs or food. Still, there have been a number of grizzly bear attacks in the province in recent years.
A grizzly bear attacked a group of students and teachers in the Bella Coola valley in November 2025. Two people were critically injured, and two were seriously hurt. Others were treated on the scene and released, CBC News reported at the time. The bear was described as "aggressive," . The incident deeply shook the local community.
In October 2025, a in British Columbia's McGregor Mountain area, northeast of Prince George. One of the hikers was transported to the hospital in critical condition and died a few weeks later due to complications from the injuries. The grizzly bear was later found dead, according to the B.C. Conservation Officer Service.
A man suffered "significant injuries," including broken bones and lacerations, after being in British Columbia's Elkford region in May 2024. He was able to shoot the bear to defend himself. The animal was later found dead. The man was flown to an area hospital for treatment.

content:
Across regional Australia – that is, populated regions outside of the major metropolitan areas – renewable energy developments have become sites of increasingly contentious political debate. While concerns about land use, environmental impacts, and community consultation are often legitimate, opposition to these projects also operates within an information environment shaped by organized resistance to climate policy, concentrated media ownership, and transnational political networks.
Understanding this environment requires looking beyond individual instances of misinformation to examine how particular narratives are produced, legitimized, and circulated.
Climate skepticism cannot be explained simply as a failure of scientific communication. Ideological barriers to accepting climate science have been cultivated by influential actors seeking to undermine scientific consensus for personal gain. Decades of research have documented how fossil-fuel interests have created a professional ecosystem of political advocacy organizations, conservative think tanks and media corporations for this.
In Australia, these relationships have been examined through research on corporate influence over climate policy, conservative political networks and the connections between fossil capital and neoliberal advocacy.
As human-caused climate change has grown more and more incontrovertible, contemporary obstruction evolved to increasingly contest climate solutions rather than denying climate change itself. These discourses of climate delay include arguments that overstate transition costs, promote continued fossil-fuel dependence, or defer action through speculative technological alternatives. Such narratives are also evident in mainstream television coverage internationally.
This distinction is important because legitimate concerns about renewable infrastructure can be selectively amplified or reframed to suggest that climate action is economically destructive, technologically unworkable, or politically illegitimate.
The circulation of climate delay narratives reflects a broader transformation in the relationship between journalism and political advocacy in an increasingly transnational digital information system. Hyperpartisan news organizations operate as platform-native political actors, producing content for recommendation systems, audience engagement, and transnational distribution. Rather than simply reporting on political controversies, these outlets interpret otherwise distinct disputes through a highly partisan lens, connecting them to recurring narratives of government overreach, institutional distrust, and opposition to progressive social and environmental policies.
News24, formerly Sky News Australia, exemplifies this convergence. As part of Murdoch’s media empire, News Corp, the outlet has a long history of producing and amplifying climate misinformation. Its substantial YouTube presence, combined with regional free-to-air distribution, enables political commentary to circulate between international digital audiences and Australian regional communities. This creates a distinctive capacity to import narratives developed within overseas culture wars, adapt them to Australian political circumstances, and elevate local controversies into matters of wider ideological significance.
Our own research examined more than 114,000 videos and 51 million comments across Sky News Australia, Fox News, GB News, and Rebel News, identifying substantial overlap between their commenting audiences. More than 56 percent of accounts commenting on Sky News Australia’s YouTube channel also commented on Fox News during the study period. This is the result of a strategy to target the highly profitable U.S. audience, potentially facilitating the importation of U.S. culture war narratives into regional Australia. While these findings do not establish direct persuasion or coordinated editorial activity, they demonstrate how ostensibly national news outlets participate in interconnected transnational political environments.
These relationships are especially consequential for climate and energy debates. A dispute over a regional wind farm or transmission corridor can be situated within a much broader narrative about metropolitan elites, government incompetence, or the supposed failure of climate policy, which has been constructed over decades by a right-wing alternative information system heavily influenced by fossil fuel interests.
Conversely, controversies originating overseas can provide ready-made arguments, political identities and rhetorical strategies for interpreting Australian developments. Hyperpartisan news outlets are important vectors in both directions, translating local grievances into internationally recognizable political conflicts while supplying those conflicts with new examples and apparent evidence.
Communication surrounding the proposed World Heritage “in danger” listing of the Great Barrier Reef further illustrates this process, with research identifying connections between News Corp outlets, conservative think tanks, political actors and climate-sceptic online communities. As one example, commentary originating in The Australian was republished through advocacy organizations and international websites, extending its circulation beyond the newspaper’s original audience. The case demonstrates how established news organizations can supply narratives with journalistic credibility while interconnected political networks facilitate their wider distribution.
The significance of these networks extends beyond the circulation of misleading information. Research into climate obstruction documents how corporations, mediated through industry associations, think tanks and political actors, seek to influence public debate through interconnected advocacy and communication systems.
Astroturfing is one expression of this process, disguising organized political interests as grassroots participation. Evidence from a study looking into decision-making during the 2025 federal election identified advertising practices that obscured connections between political campaigns, lobbyists and apparently independent community organizations.
Hyperpartisan news outlets perform a related, although distinct, function. They can elevate local grievances into national political controversies, selectively reinforce narratives aligned with established commercial or ideological interests, and present these interpretations through the familiar conventions of journalism. News Corp plays a longstanding role in contesting climate science and policy, including its connections with conservative think tanks such as the IPA and fossil-fuel interests. Through this process, arguments favorable to fossil-fuel interests can acquire the apparent independence and authority of news coverage before being recirculated through political and social media networks.
For regional Australia, these dynamics complicate an already difficult energy transition. Genuine concerns about land use, environmental impacts, and community benefits can be easily hijacked by a fossil-fuel dominated transnational information system.
Thus, transforming local disagreements into wider confrontations over political identity and institutional legitimacy, further delaying an appropriate, scientific response to human-caused climate change. Understanding and communicating who produces these narratives, how they travel, and whose interests they advance is therefore essential to protecting meaningful democratic participation in decisions about Australia’s energy future.
Originally published under Creative Commons by 360info™.
summary: Research traces how partisan outlets link climate-delay narratives, fossil-fuel interests, and audiences, reshaping regional energy debates and public trust.

content:
The Iranian regime was quick to label the resounding in the midterm elections as evidence of American voters rejecting the costly war he launched with Israel more than eight months ago.
Spain's leader called it a sign of a global, right-wing populist "wave" crumbling, and Russia acknowledged that it "could complicate relations with the U.S."
Below is a look at those statements and other reactions from foreign leaders and figures, including some hopeful leaders as elections loom in other countries.
Iran
A statement attributed to Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei on Wednesday made it clear that Tehran is not expecting the outcome of the U.S. elections to change Washington's approach more than eight months into its war with Iran:
"If there are still people who harbor even the slightest hope for a change in behavior or for party and factional shifts within the system of domination, or who believe that by making concessions to America they can dissuade it from hostility toward the Iranian nation, they are gravely mistaken," the statement published on Khamenei's official website said.
Earlier, Iran's chief negotiator said the results reflected Americans' rejection of the war with his country.
"Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message," Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said in a post on X. He cited the increased cost of living, or "conscience," as two possible reasons for the widespread Republican losses.
"If the U.S. govt betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare," Ghalibaf added as a warning.
Russia
In Russia, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said he hoped President Trump would still be able to "continue his peace-making efforts" in the wake of the U.S. elections.
A new round of working-level talks between Russia and Ukraine, brokered by the U.S., is scheduled to take place Nov. 10-11 in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.
Mr. Trump has pushed Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy hard this year to accept a peace deal that many argue would strongly favor Moscow, with Kyiv likely having to allow Russia to maintain control over some of the territory it has occupied in Ukraine during the grueling four-year war.
Several previous rounds of U.S.-brokered talks have yielded prisoner exchanges, and a recent local ceasefire credited to first lady Melania Trump and Pope Leo brought calm to one southern city occupied by Russia, but there has been no indication that Putin is prepared to abandon his demand to unilaterally seize Ukrainian territory as part of a deal to end the war.
Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov noted Wednesday that Moscow has long had strained interactions with Democrats, saying the U.S. party's "core approach to relations with Russia is extremely negative."
Ryabkov said Russia's foreign policy would not be influenced by the election results, and its stance on Ukraine in particular would not change.
There was no immediate reaction from Ukraine's government to the U.S. election results.
Spain
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, among the most vocal European critics of the war with Iran and other Trump administration policies, welcomed the results, saying in a post on X that Americans had "voted against policies that only impoverish. Against hatred. Against sexism."
Sanchez, who will face his own country's electorate in a Nov. 29 election, called the U.S. results further evidence of a global right-wing populist wave crumbling, and he said he believed a similar result would follow in Spain.
"It . It just happened in the US. And it will happen soon in Spain," he predicted.
European Union
Top European Union diplomat Kaja Kallas voiced hope on Wednesday she that the new U.S. Congress would increase support for Ukraine and ramp up pressure on Russia with Democrats now in charge of both the House and the Senate.
Kallas said Europe and the United States "are much stronger together" in any efforts to push Russia to end its full-scale invasion.
European Parliament Vice President Christel Schaldemose, in an earlier post on X, called the election results "wild."
"Not because everything now changes for the better, but because it could benefit the support for Ukraine, the green transition, and relations with the rest of the world," she said, adding that the EU "must continue the course of standing stronger and standing on its own two feet. That's not up for debate."
United Kingdom
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham's reaction to the walloping doled out to President Trump's Republican Party in the U.S. midterms was largely apolitical.
"President Trump has accepted the results, and I feel the world has an opportunity now to unite around the issue that is affecting us all, and that's the cost of living," Burnham told reporters in London on Wednesday, adding that prices could not be reduced until the U.S. war with Iran "is resolved."
South Africa
South African President Cyril Ramaphosa told reporters Wednesday that the U.S. election results would "introduce a new era in world relations."
"We have seen that the Democrats have taken control of the Senate and of the House, and the people of America have spoken," he said.
The Trump administration has had tense relations with South Africa, of allowing the persecution of the country's White Afrikaner population and inviting its members to — an opening that some 17,000 have sought to take advantage of.
Mr. Trump has alleged that Afrikaners face a "genocide" in South Africa. In a tense Oval Office meeting last year, he confronted Ramaphosa on the claims, showing him a video that spotlighted murders of farmers in the country.
The claims, long pushed by Elon Musk, have been strongly disputed. A 60 Minutes who that they are facing a genocide and said murders on farms were linked to a broader crime problem in South Africa that harms people of all races.
Germany
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said Wednesday that he expected cooperation between Europe's single largest economy and the U.S. to become "broader and perhaps more interesting" with the Democrats now in control of the House and Senate.
On U.S. support for Ukraine amid Russia's ongoing full-scale invasion, Wadephul said he was optimistic that both parties in the U.S. Congress would now engage more with each other to boost backing for Ukraine's government.
France
French Economy Minister Roland Lescure declined on Wednesday, during an interview with the BFM television network, to predict whether President Trump would "accept" the rebuke by American voters or stick to the policies widely perceived as having precipitated the midterm Republican defeat.
"Either he decides to rise above the fray — acknowledging that changes are necessary, particularly regarding gasoline prices, which directly affect people — and, I might add, he tones down his international involvement; or he does not," said Lescure, adding that it was "something we will need to keep an eye on in the coming days."
Norway
Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere on Wednesday called the U.S. election results "a powerful political signal about a change of course among American voters."
"Voices are now emerging in American politics that are closer to us than the president and the administration have stood for, for example on climate and environment, and in foreign policy and development aid policy."
This article will be updated with additional international reaction.
summary: Iran says the U.S. election results reflect a rejection of war and Spain's leader says it's another sign of a right-wing populist wave falling apart.

content:
The emergence of the “Squad” alongside the Quad reflects a changing security landscape in the Indo-Pacific, wherein regional cooperation is being shaped by nontraditional security challenges and the imperative of military deterrence. The defense ministers’ meeting of the Squad – the United States, Japan, Australia and the Philippines – on the sidelines of the 13th ASEAN Defense Ministers’ Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) in Cebu, Philippines on October 28 underscored this emerging trend. The meeting also took place alongside separate engagements involving the Quad partners – the United States, Japan, Australia, and India – highlighting how overlapping partnerships are focusing on distinct strategic purposes.
The Squad showcases the operational dimension of Indo-Pacific security cooperation. Its significance lies in strengthening defense coordination among the U.S. and its allies – all countries with an immediate strategic stake in the western Pacific and the South China Sea. At the meeting in Cebu, the four ministers agreed to advance defense cooperation through consultations, joint military exercises, and other initiatives. Japan’s Ministry of Defense described these efforts as contributing to regional peace and stability.
Australia’s Defense Minister Richard Marles also indicated that the discussion covered operational concepts and closer coordination among defense policy experts. These developments suggest that the Squad is moving toward more practical forms of military coordination, such as interoperability and joint exercises, that can strengthen the ability of participating countries to respond collectively to contingencies.
The Philippines’ geographical position shapes the Squad’s strategic importance. As a claimant state in the South China Sea and a U.S. treaty ally, the Philippines occupies a crucial position along the First Island Chain. Hence, greater cooperation with Japan and Australia gives Manila additional strategic partnerships, while allowing Washington to strengthen its regional posture through a network of capable partners. The grouping could therefore contribute to deterrence by raising the potential costs of coercive actions and demonstrating that challenges to regional security may also elicit a coordinated response. The Squad’s contribution to regional peace would depend on whether its enhanced capabilities are accompanied by restraint, transparency and adherence to international law.
On the other hand, although strategic coordination and maritime security remain important, Quad cooperation has also focused on nontraditional security challenges and the provision of regional public goods. These include humanitarian assistance and disaster relief, maritime domain awareness, critical and emerging technologies, health security, and resilient supply chains. This broader agenda gives the Quad a distinctive role in the Indo-Pacific. It brings together four countries – including India, which is not a U.S. treaty ally – to address shared regional challenges through practical cooperation and coordinated initiatives. The Quad’s approach is also particularly pertinent to Southeast Asia, where countries seek stronger maritime capabilities and economic resilience without wishing to become aligned with competing military blocs.
The Quad and the Squad therefore address different and overlapping dimensions of the regional security environment. While the Quad contributes to resilience and functional cooperation, the Squad is more directly oriented toward defense coordination and deterrence in a strategically sensitive maritime theater. The simultaneous meetings by the Squad and Quad partners around the Cebu ADMM-Plus raises an important question: is the emergence of explicitly defense-oriented minilateral arrangements reducing the Quad’s strategic relevance?
The answer is no, although it reflects a growing differentiation in the functions of Indo-Pacific partnerships. The Quad’s focus on nontraditional security cooperation should not be mistaken for an absence of strategic intent. Initiatives such as the Indo-Pacific Partnership for Maritime Domain Awareness demonstrate that its functional agenda can strengthen maritime surveillance, improve information-sharing, and help regional states respond to coercive activities. Nevertheless, the Quad has deliberately avoided becoming a conventional military alliance. The Squad, by contrast, provides a more focused platform for defense consultations, military exercises, and operational coordination among four countries with immediate security interests in the Western Pacific.
Importantly, the Squad’s emergence does not establish a formal division of responsibilities between the two groupings, nor does it demonstrate that the Quad has been superseded. Rather, it illustrates how countries can pursue different levels of security cooperation through overlapping arrangements. The Quad’s broader agenda and the Squad’s more concentrated deterrence function can be complementary, even as their respective approaches reflect different strategic priorities.
For regional stability, the Squad presents both opportunities and risks. Enhanced interoperability, joint exercises, and defense consultations can strengthen deterrence and reassure countries concerned about coercion in contested maritime spaces. For the Philippines, the arrangement also provides a mechanism to deepen security partnerships and improve its ability to respond to regional contingencies. However, a regional order increasingly shaped by competing minilateral groupings risks intensifying strategic mistrust. China may interpret closer military coordination along the First Island Chain as an attempt to constrain its strategic options, potentially encouraging countermeasures and further militarization. Smaller Southeast Asian countries could also face greater pressure to navigate between competing security interests.
This makes the role of ASEAN and the ADMM-Plus particularly important. Unlike exclusive minilateral arrangements, ADMM-Plus brings ASEAN members together with eight dialogue partners, including India, China, Japan, the United States, and Australia, providing a forum for defense dialogue and practical cooperation. Its continued relevance lies in maintaining communication among competing powers while promoting cooperation on shared security challenges.
In the same way, the Squad should be understood not as a replacement for the Quad but as an expression of the Indo-Pacific’s increasingly layered security architecture. The Quad seeks to strengthen regional resilience through a broad agenda of functional cooperation, while the Squad is developing a more direct role in military deterrence and maritime security. Both can contribute to regional stability, provided their activities reinforce international law, avoid unnecessary escalation and leave sufficient space for ASEAN-led diplomacy. The central challenge is not choosing between the two, but ensuring that stronger deterrence and wider regional cooperation remain complementary rather than contradictory.
summary: The Squad should be understood not as a replacement for the Quad but as an expression of the Indo-Pacific’s increasingly layered security architecture.

content:
‘ก้อง ห้วยไร่’ ลั่นเลิกเป็นสะพานบุญ หลังเจอบทเรียนราคาแพง ให้กำลังใจ ‘เบลล่า’ เชื่อบริจาคด้วยจิตบริสุทธิ์
หลังจากนักร้องหนุ่ม ก้อง ห้วยไร่ เข้ารับการผ่าตัดใหญ่ที่หัวเข่า ท่ามกลางความห่วงใยจากภรรยาและเพื่อนพ้องในวงการ ล่าสุด “ก้อง” ร่วมให้สัมภาษณ์ภาพยนตร์คอเมดี้ฟอร์มยักษ์จาก Netflix เรื่อง แก๊งโอเวอร์ ณ โรงภาพยนตร์ พารากอน ซีนีเพล็กซ์ ชั้น 5 ศูนย์การค้าสยามพารากอน อัพเดตสุขภาพและสภาพจิตใจ พร้อมเปิดใจปมบริจาคเงินให้กับมูลนิธิองค์กรทำดี
สุขภาพเป็นยังไงบ้าง?
“โอ้โห แย่มากเลยครับ ผมเลยกลายเป็นแพนิก เวลาเสิร์ชไปดูคลิปที่พี่ๆ เพื่อนๆ นักฟุตบอล นักกีฬาเตะกัน เล่นกันแรงๆ แล้วมันรู้สึกกลัวเลยครับ แล้วก็รู้สึกว่าทำทำไมวะ เขารู้ไหมว่าเวลาไปผ่าตัดมันทรมานแค่ไหน ทั้งสุขภาพจิตก็พังตามไปด้วย มันตามไปยังไง คุณเคยเล่นกีฬาแล้วออกกำลังกายไม่ได้ไหมครับ ทรมานมาก เพราะฉะนั้นอย่าเป็นนะครับ เอ็นไขว้หน้าขาดเนี่ย”
ตอนนี้สามารถกลับไปสนามฟุตบอลได้หรือยัง?
“ไม่เลยครับ หมอขอ 2 ปี ตอนนี้เพิ่งผ่านมาได้ อันนี้ด้วยความไม่รู้ คือจริงๆ มันต้องพัก 6 เดือนเป็นขั้นต่ำ ผมพัก 15 วัน คือล็อกคิวว่าไม่รับคอนเสิร์ต 15 วัน แล้วหลังจากนั้นก็นั่งเก้าอี้ร้องเพลงครับ”
ตอนนี้มีอาการอย่างไรบ้าง?
“คือถ้าเกิดว่าย่ออย่างนี้มันจะไม่ได้เลยครับ ยืนนี่ก็ต้องยืนขาขวา ต้องใช้พี่หมอนวดมาคลายเส้นขาขวา เพราะเหมือนน้ำหนักมันมาที่ขาขวา เสร็จปุ๊บขาซ้ายรีบ กล้ามเนื้อที่เคยมีมันฝ่อ ตอนนี้กำลังเร่งพยายามขึ้นครับ”
ต้องใช้คนช่วยทำกายภาพบำบัดใช่ไหม?
“ใช่ครับ ต้องใช้พี่ๆ มาทำกายภาพ เพราะขี้เกียจ เราก็นอนให้เขาดึงแข้งดึงขาไปครับ
อันนี้หนักสุดไหม?
“หนักสุดไหมสำหรับชีวิตผมว่ามันก็ไม่หนักเท่านี้แหละ แต่ถ้าเรื่องสุขภาพ ผมว่าอันนี้หนักที่สุด เพราะเป็นการผ่าตัดใหญ่ และผมเพิ่งรู้ว่าหลังผ่าตัดจะหนาวผิดปกติ ผมไม่รู้ว่ามันเกิดจากอะไร”
มีวิธีเยียวยาจิตใจตัวเองอย่างไรบ้าง?
“ผมว่าอยากเตะบอล อยากออกกำลังกายกับเพื่อน มันลำบากมากกว่า เห็นเพื่อนเล่นบอลการกุศลโน่นนี่นั่น แล้วเราก็ได้แต่มอง กลายเป็นจิตตก”
นอกจากการเตะฟุตบอล มีอะไรที่ช่วยทดแทนได้บ้าง?
“แฟนเพลงอย่างเดียวเลย ไปร้องเพลงแล้วก็ไปโต้ตอบกับเขา ซึ่งเป็นนักร้องนิสัยไม่ดี ด่าแฟนเพลง แต่แฟนเพลงปรบมือให้ (เพราะเราด่าเขาแล้วเขาไม่โกรธ?) คือเขารู้แหละว่าเราไม่ได้ด่าเพราะเราโกรธ เราด่าหยอกๆ เขา แต่ผมก็ดูนะ ไม่ใช่ว่าด่ามั่ว คนนี้ทรงนี้เล่นไม่ได้ว่ะ น่าจะไม่สนุกกับเรา เราก็เลือกๆ อยู่ครับ”
ภรรยาว่าอย่างไรบ้างเรื่องการดูแล?
“ก็เป็นแม่บ้านที่ต้องทำทุกอย่าง พอเห็นว่าสุขภาพจิตเราแย่ เขาก็อยากให้เราสนุก เพราะว่าไปทำงานก็มีคนมารอดูเรา ก็พยายามไม่นั่งให้มากที่สุด เวลาไปเล่นคอนเสิร์ตครับ”
แต่น้องๆ ก็เป็นห่วง อย่าง เบิ้ล ปทุมราช?
“เป็นห่วง เพราะมันรู้ว่าผมเป็นคนชอบเล่นกีฬา แล้วก็คุยกันหลังไมค์กันอย่างนี้ครับ ที่ห่างกันเพราะว่าเขาไปเป็นดารา (แล้วเราล่ะ เราเป็นอะไร ?) เป็นนักร้อง เราเป็นนักร้อง เราก็ต้องทำงาน (แอ๊กติ้งร้องไห้) ตั้งแต่คบพี่ณเดชน์ ไม่คุยกับกูเลย (อันนี้คุณดราม่า?) ลูกเมียมาแล้ว เฮ้ย เป็นไง พ่อบอกแล้วพ่อเป็นดารา ลูกไม่รู้ เพราะว่าซีเจมอลล์เขายิงแอดที่ผมเต้น ครูถาม พ่อทำงานอะไร บอกว่าขายของอยู่ซีเจมอลล์”
ให้กำลังใจเบลล่า (ราณี) หน่อย ตอนนี้น้องโดนเรียกไปให้ข้อมูลเกี่ยวกับการบริจาคเงินให้กับมูลนิธิองค์กรทำดี?
“ผมว่าให้กำลังใจ ผมว่าดีด้วยซ้ำ เพราะน้องเป็นคนที่มีชื่อเสียง เป็นคนที่รู้จักกันเยอะ การที่น้องบริจาคด้วยจิตอันบริสุทธิ์ แฟนๆ เห็นว่าขนาดเบลล่ายังบริจาค เราไปบริจาคเติมกันเข้าไปดีกว่า ผมก็เลยมองว่าน้องต้องไปแหละดีแล้วครับ แต่ผมไม่ก้าวล่วงเรื่องคนอื่นนะครับ เพราะผมเข้าใจอยู่ แต่ว่าไม่เป็นไร เพราะเราก็เจอกันบ่อยๆ กับน้องเบลล่าครับ”
ได้คุยอะไรกับน้องบ้างไหม?
“โอ้โห ไม่ได้คุยเลยครับ ส่วนมากคุยกับภรรยาผม เขาสนิทกัน เขาสนิทกับภรรยาผม เวลาเขามาเจอกันผมก็ต้องขึ้นไปนอนแล้ว เพราะเวลาผู้หญิงคุยกัน เราก็ไม่รู้จะนั่งฟังอะไร เรื่องผู้หญิง”
อย่างก้องบริจาคให้มูลนิธินี้ไหม?
“ช่างมันเถอะครับ บริจาคด้วยจิตบริสุทธิ์ไปแล้วก็ช่างมันเถอะ แล้วแต่เขา ก็เป็นวิบากของเขา ผมก็ตั้งใจแล้วว่าทุกวันนี้กลายไปเป็นไม่รับเงินจากหน้าเวทีมาเป็นปีแล้ว (เพราะดราม่า?) ผมเอาเงินของแฟนเพลงไปมอบให้คนที่เขาไม่ได้เอาไปทำจริง รู้สึกผิดเลยครับ ก็เลยบอกว่าหลังจากนี้ไม่ต้องให้ผมนะ ผมจะเอาเงินจากค่าตัวนั่นแหละ เพราะเจ้าภาพให้มาเยอะแล้ว (ก็คือเลิกเป็นสะพานบุญแล้ว ไม่เอาแล้ว?) ไม่เป็นสะพานบุญแล้ว ไม่รับเงินจากแฟนเพลงแล้ว เพราะถึงเขาจะให้โดยเสน่หาก็ตาม แต่ว่าจุดประสงค์ก็พลาดไปแล้ว”
ถ้าเกิดเวลาทำความดีบ่อยๆ พอมาเกิดเหตุการณ์แบบนี้ขึ้น เรามีความรู้สึกอย่างไรบ้าง มันเสื่อมศรัทธา?
“ผมว่าไม่เสื่อมครับ คนที่ตั้งใจคือคนที่ตั้งใจ เหมือนข่าวพระหรือข่าวใครก็ตาม มันเป็นแค่บุคคลคนเดียว มันจะเปลี่ยนไม่ได้ แต่คนที่เขารอความช่วยเหลือมันก็ต้องมี ถามว่าเขาช่วยจริงไหม ทุกคนช่วยจริงนะ เขาช่วยจริงๆ แต่ส่วนผิดก็คือผิด ส่วนถูกเราก็ต้องชื่นชม ส่วนผิดก็รับวิบากกรรมของตัวเองไป ผมคิดว่าไม่อยากให้มองว่าต่อไปจะไม่มีใครกล้าทำแล้วนะ เพราะโลกมันมีกฎหมายนะ ถ้าอยากทำให้มันไม่ถูกต้อง สังคมหรือกฎหมายเขาก็สั่งสอนเราเองครับ”
กังวลไหม เพราะช่วงน้ำท่วมก็เคยเปิดรับบริจาคเช่นกัน?
“พี่ก้องตัดสินใจโดยใช้วิธีการเอาเงินสดออกจากบัญชีทั้งหมด เบิกก้อนเดียว และให้เห็นทุกบาททุกสตางค์ ตอนที่ไปมอบต้องมีการถ่ายภาพ มีการรับจริง แล้วก็เอาลูกพี่ไปประกันตัว คือพี่โอม “ลูกพี่ครับ ไปช่วยผมหน่อย ไปประกันตัวให้ผมหน่อย” ก็ไปวางไว้ลงโรงเรียนละ 1- 2 ล้าน ซึ่งเขาต้องเห็นเราใช้ ผมไม่สามารถรู้หรอกว่าโรงเรียนเขาเอาไปใช้จริงไหม แต่ผมก็เอาไปวางให้เขาได้เห็นครับ”
แสดงว่าโปร่งใส?
“โปร่งใสครับ ธนาคารกรุงไทยจะน่ารักกับผมเสมอ เพราะว่าพี่ต้องปิดการโอนเข้าโอนออกกับผมตอนนี้ เดี๋ยวนี้ แล้วเอาเงินออกมาก้อนเดียว ทั้งหมดเป็นกี่บาทกี่สตางค์ มันมีภาพในโซเชียลทั้งหมด แล้วเราก็จัดการ”
สำหรับเราคิดไหมว่าหลังจากนี้จะไม่รับช่วยบริจาค?
“ผมว่าโอนตรงดีที่สุด แต่พอเป็นอย่างนี้นะ มันก็อดคิดไม่ได้ เพราะโอนตรงไปเขาเอาไปทำอะไรก็ยังไม่รู้ เอาเป็นว่าเท่าที่ไหวนะครับทุกคน มนุษย์ทุกคนเกิดมาเป็นสัตว์สังคม มันเป็นเรื่องปกติที่จะเห็นอกเห็นใจเพื่อนมนุษย์ด้วยกัน แต่รักตัวเองไว้ก่อนนะครับทุกคน รักตัวเองไว้ก่อน เอาตัวเอง เอาครอบครัวเราให้มีความสุขซะก่อน ก่อนที่จะไปช่วยคนอื่น เพราะสุดท้ายแล้วในวันที่เราแย่ คนที่จะช่วยเราได้มีแค่คนเดียวคือตัวเราจริงๆ ครับ เพราะฉะนั้นคนที่อยากทำความดี อย่าหมดศรัทธา ทำต่อ เป็นแบบนี้ต่อไป แต่อะไรที่มันถูกต้องต้องให้มันถูกต้องแล้วทีนี้ คุณเห็นชัดอยู่แล้วว่าผลตามมามันเป็นอย่างไร สังคมมันชัดขึ้นนะ ก็เลยแบบว่าอยากทำก็ทำต่อ แต่ต้องชัด เพราะหลังจากนี้คุณจะยากหน่อย ใครที่ทำอะไรไม่ชัด”
summary: ‘ก้อง ห้วยไร่’ ลั่นเลิกเป็นสะพานบุญ หลังเจอ […]

content:
The much-hailed ban on drugs by the Taliban since April 2022 notwithstanding, opium production in Afghanistan is again on the rise. The latest findings of the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) on opium production in Afghanistan are revealing. The era of Taliban success in controlling and diminishing opium production seems to be over. To the contrary, production has jumped fivefold in a year, with a new growing area away from the traditional southwest.
Behind the steep rise are intertwining stories of international demand, desperation and adaptation by poverty-stricken farmers, and the failure not just of the country’s de facto authorities but also of the international community to keep production low.
The latest UNODC report highlighted how, despite claims of the eradication of 22,000 hectares of poppy this year by the Taliban, the area planted grew by 330 percent to more than 43,000 hectares, up from about 10,000 hectares in 2025. Estimated production also rose by 400 percent, from about 300 tonnes to just under 1,500 tonnes. The report pointed to the role of poverty and lack of alternative crops in driving the increase, forcing farmers to adopt innovative methods to evade Taliban scrutiny. With opium stockpiles fast emptying due to constant demand from Europe, and a lack of any other country capable of filling supply needs, a back-to-the-future moment is at hand for Afghan opium production.
Several underlying structural factors make total elimination a mere fallacy.
First is the expansion of production. UNODC says that cultivation has spread to 16 of Afghanistan’s 34 provinces, up from 11 in 2025. The new provinces now cultivating poppies are Balkh, Daykundi, Farah, Herat, Laghman, and Nangarhar. Only Zabul became poppy-free, which results in a net increase of five provinces now growing opium poppy. UNODC has historically classified provinces with less than 100 hectares of cultivation as poppy-free.
The emergence of Afghanistan’s northeastern provinces as the main growing areas for poppy sheds further light on the complex linkages between the narco-economy, illicit networks, and the absence of state control.
UNODC identifies two provinces – Badakhshan and Takhar – as accounting for 76 percent of total cultivation in 2026. The remaining 14 provinces are therefore marginal players. Breaking this down further reveals that Badakhshan’s 29,482 hectares of identified poppy-growing area amounts to 68 percent of such areas in the entire country. Takhar, on the other hand, contributes only 8 percent. Notably, only 3,561 hectares of Badakhshan grew poppy in 2021, before the Taliban captured power. That represents a 728 percent increase in just five years. More interestingly, not long ago, in 2025, only 6,639 hectares were under poppy cultivation in the province. That amounts to an increase of 344 percent in a single year.
In percentage terms, the rise of poppy cultivation in Takhar is even more explosive. The province was completely poppy-free in 2021. By 2025, though, poppy was being grown on 274 hectares, making it a minor contributor. But in 2026, it registered a 1,100 percent increase, reaching 3,400 hectares.
Badakhshan, which borders Pakistan’s restive Gilgit-Baltistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provinces, and adjacent Takhar, are the central actors in the resurgence of Afghanistan’s narco-economy, even as they are not the only areas where poppy cultivation is returning.
Helmand and Kandahar, both in the traditional southwest poppy-growing area, have registered 400 and 300 percent growth, respectively.
The rising resentment of the farmers against the Taliban in Badakhshan and Takhar, local collusion, as well as the rise of anti-Taliban armed resistance, probably explain why Taliban efforts to rein in opium production have shown little progress. Whether eradication is also failing in other provinces, including the spiritual capital of Kandahar, remains unanswered. If the Taliban figure of eradication of 22,000 hectares of poppy is to be believed, the net increase in overall area would amount to 55,000 hectares and not only the 33,000 that UNODC estimates.
Since 2023, UNODC has emphasized its “Alternative Development Program,” which works with communities in Afghanistan and aims to encourage farmers to move away from illicit crop cultivation and in favor of licit crops. This includes measures such as orchard establishment and poultry production, as well as management support. It is evident, however, that these programs have not been able to make much impact on the ground.
UNODC’s latest report refers to the adaptability of the farmers and the involvement of the non-local middlemen in the rise of poppy cultivation in the northeast. Cultivation in small patches that are hidden within cereal fields or inside walled compounds could be contributing factors, but these cannot explain why such a phenomenon that’s known to UNODC remains hidden from the omnipresent Taliban.
Is there a nexus between cash-strapped Taliban operatives and other warlords, and the narcotics smugglers in Pakistan? Sources in Zabul, the province that reported no poppy cultivation in 2026, told local media that in fact some Taliban fighters, alongside drug traffickers, are involved in the collection, processing, and smuggling of drugs in the province, a sign that the existing illicit network is growing.
Further, it is hard to imagine that the poppy – raw and processed – from Badakhshan and Takhar isn’t crossing over into Pakistan through the porous border. Balochistan appears to have become the main hub of opium cultivation in the Afghanistan-Pakistan-Iran border region. Experts have also warned that the tri-border area comprising Pakistan’s southwestern province of Balochistan and Iran’s southeastern province of Sistan-Baluchistan, both bordering Afghanistan, have witnessed a sharp rise in poppy cultivation in recent years. Similarly, are the anti-Taliban resistance forces, who claim to have made Badakhshan one of their primary areas of operation, also involved in the trade to finance their war?
The resurgence of opium in Afghanistan is more than a statistical reversal. The Taliban ban on all cultivation of opium poppy, celebrated as a rare success, rests on coercion rather than on any change in the underlying structural conditions that drive farmers to cultivate poppy. Moreover, the Taliban have done little to break the illicit networks sustaining this shadow economy, including cash flows through the hawala systems. Statistical achievements have little meaning in the absence of changes in ground realities – a point that the explosion of coca production in Colombia could speak to.
For Afghanistan’s neighbors and the wider world, the lesson is daunting. Steady demand for drugs will ensure there is a market for revived supply, while an international community that offers neither meaningful development support nor engagement as to alternatives leaves farmers with few options. Lasting reduction in poppy cultivation can only result from a combined effort by the de facto authorities and the international community to provide viable alternative livelihoods, transparent governance in the provinces where cultivation is surging, and cooperation across borders to choke off the trafficking routes. Until then, the cycle of the illicit narco-economy will keep reinventing itself.
summary: The resurgence of opium in Afghanistan is more than a statistical reversal.

content:
Late last month, Pakistan announced that Taiwanese airlines such as China Airlines and EVA Air would not be allowed to fly over the country. This took place after an announcement by Minister of Defense Khawaja Asif, whose responsibilities also entail overflight privileges. Asif claimed that the ban was on the basis of Pakistan’s One China policy.
It was the first time that a country had revoked overflight privileges for Taiwanese airlines on the basis of a claimed One China policy. Previously, EVA Air and China Airlines – which, despite its name, is Taiwan’s national carrier, not to be confused with the Chinese flag carrier Air China – had been cleared for overflight privileges by Pakistan’s Civil Aviation Authority from October 28 of this year through March 27, 2027.
The move by Pakistan did not last long, however, with the country reversing course soon after. Taiwanese airlines continue to enjoy overflight privileges to Pakistan.
It remains unclear why the decision was made by Pakistan’s government in the first place – and why it was reversed shortly after. It is possible that Pakistan did not anticipate international pressure after the announcement which may have occurred behind the scenes. Likewise, it is not clear as to whether it was the Pakistan government’s decision to revoke Taiwan’s overflight privileges or whether this came after a request from Beijing.
The move came about a month ahead of Taiwan’s local elections in late November. In other countries, China is indeed seeking to apply pressure to Taiwan in the lead-up to the polls. In past months, there have been reports of Taiwanese nationals being denied admittance to Uganda and Kenya, on the basis that their Taiwanese passports were not issued by Beijing, and thus not considered valid travel documents.
In August, four Taiwanese in Uganda had their passports confiscated, though eventually they were returned. In June, two Taiwanese delegates to the 11th Our Ocean Conference in Mombasa, Kenya, were refused admittance to the conference because their Taiwanese passports were considered “invalid.” They subsequently had their passports and cell phones confiscated and were detained for 20 hours, though they were later released. Despite conflicting reports afterward, it appears Taiwanese are still able to enter Kenya using their passports.
Pakistan may have been the first to threaten a wholesale ban on Taiwanese airlines overflying its airspace, but other countries have revoked overflight privileges to specific Taiwanese aircraft, apparently at China’s behest. In April, a trip by President Lai Ching-te to Eswatini, Taiwan’s only African diplomatic ally, was abruptly cancelled. Lai had planned to visit Eswatini for the 40th anniversary of King Mswati III’s accession to the throne, which also marked Mswati’s 58th birthday. The trip was cancelled after Madagascar, Mauritius, and the Seychelles revoked overflight privileges for Lai’s aircraft.
Although details remain scarce, the Taiwanese government has claimed that the Chinese government threatened to revoke debt cancellation for these countries if they allowed the passage of Lai’s aircraft. It is possible that China may have exercised similar leverage over Pakistan. If so, this would suggest that restricting Taiwan’s access to airspace has become a new tactic in China’s playbook for pressuring Taiwan.
For its part, the Lai administration has sought to link Pakistan’s actions to Taiwan’s exclusion from the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), the United Nations body responsible for global aviation safety. Taiwanese governments have long called for Taiwan’s admission to the ICAO, raising the dangers for international aviation safety when a large aviation hub such as Taiwan is excluded from the global body for civil aviation.
It is also possible that the Pakistan government revoked overflight privileges for EVA Air and China Airlines of its own initiative as a means of strengthening ties with Beijing. For countries that wish to build stronger ties with China, hitting out at Taiwan is a way to signal their dedication to Beijing.
In the same way, vocal support for Taiwan can be used to signal a desire for closer ties with the United States. For instance, the governments of countries in Eastern Europe such as Lithuania showed support for Taiwan through actions such as donating vaccines during the COVID-19 pandemic as part of broader signaling efforts to indicate alignment with the United States, its Western European allies, and NATO.
Pakistan claimed that its actions were in compliance with its One China policy. Chinese government rhetoric implies the existence of a unitary One China policy or One China principle as an international consensus – sometimes with the claim that this was codified in international law by way of U.N. Resolution 2758. Citing the One China policy or One China principle has become for China to justify any number of moves against Taiwan. In reality, each country has a different and distinctive One China policy.
China often attempts to create the perception that it is already internationally recognized as having sovereignty over Taiwan. Chinese embassies abroad have sometimes been accused of seeking to take credit for the actions of the Taiwanese representative offices in assisting Taiwanese citizens with repatriation or evacuation. Taiwan maintains representative offices – often termed economic and cultural offices – in lieu of embassies in countries that it does not have formal relations with. Attempting to take credit for such actions would be a means of asserting that China’s embassies are internationally recognized as responsible for Taiwanese citizens abroad.
China has used incidents of Taiwanese nationals being extradited to China similarly. Taiwanese nationals are sometimes extradited to China to face charges because they committed acts of fraud against Chinese citizens. Beijing uses such cases to try to depict the international justice system as considering Taiwan part of China.
At times, China’s efforts have been used to intimidate. For example, last year, during a period that saw trips to Europe by a number of prominent Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) politicians, the Chinese government attempted to create the perception that it would arrest DPP legislator and current Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen during Shen’s travels in Europe through Interpol. The Chinese government also claimed to have a criminal investigation on Shen ongoing in Chongqing. For its part, Interpol stated that it would not act on political disputes. Nevertheless, China has routinely been accused of seeking to weaponize Interpol “red notices” in order to target political dissidents.
Attempting to push for the revocation of overflight privileges for Taiwanese airlines, however, would be a new tactic for China. It’s worth watching to see if Pakistan ever actually institutes such a ban, and if other countries decide to follow suit.
summary: Pakistan announced that Taiwanese airlines would not be allowed to fly over the country, before abruptly rescinding the change. Is this a new strategy from Beijing?

Belfast Trust took possession of the new maternity hospital in March 2024
Published
Almost £20m in additional costs due to problems at two Belfast Health Trust buildings has been described as "such terrible waste".
Newly-discovered issues with the Belfast maternity hospital could add almost £10m to the project's spiralling costs, while the amount spent on repairs and rehousing patients at the Acute Mental Health facility has now reached £9.4m.
Daniel McCrossan, who chairs the Public Accounts Committee, said: "We can't see such waste, such terrible waste, within our public sector and then still go to London and demand more [money]."
The Department of Health (DoH) said the extra building costs are "disappointing" but it is essential they are "completed and delivered".
The maternity building on the Royal Victoria Hospital (RVH) site is already tens of millions of pounds over budget and more than a decade behind schedule. The new costs mean the project will exceed £100m.
It is understood the latest problem at the maternity hospital has been caused by chemical flushing aimed at dealing with the original issue of bacteria in the water system.
The flushing process has caused damage to the pipework, with more than 2,200 defective valves needing replaced.
A report seen by the BBC estimates a repair bill of £7.8m, with an option of 24-hour contractor working bringing that close to £10m. Work to replace the valves is now under way.
Stormont's Public Accounts Committee oversees public spending in Northern Ireland.
SDLP MLA McCrossan said "the buck stops with the Department of Health".
"There needs to be some accountability here when it comes to the use, and indeed misuse, of public money where wastage could have been prevented."
McCrossan added that every pound counts because "it is public money".
"There needs to be very clear accountability here and we need a reassurance because we've sought this - when are these facilities going to actually open to benefit the taxpayer whose money has been invested in building it?
"When are patients going to get the benefit out of using these facilities which they're designed for?
"And ultimately, how much more are we going to stick sticking plasters over problems instead of grabbing the bull by the horns and getting these things done?"
Belfast Trust 'cannot provide further update'
The new maternity facility is due to replace the existing Royal Jubilee maternity hospital at the Royal Victoria Hospital, but the opening date remains in doubt because of the ongoing repair issues.
The building was handed over to the Belfast Trust in March 2024, but the discovery of the potentially dangerous pseudomonas bacterium in the water system and other problems has meant the hospital has remained closed.
An investigation by trust managers into the building handover and subsequent water system issues was launched earlier this year. The BBC understands it will report this month.
In Freedom of Information responses to the BBC, the Belfast Trust refused to say if the repair costs were being met by relevant building contractors or from taxpayer money.
In a series of questions from the BBC, the trust repeatedly answered: "The trust and its legal representatives continue to engage with independent experts on matters of liability and cannot provide a further update currently."
The new maternity hospital at the Royal Victoria Hospital pictured in 2024
In a statement, Belfast Trust said the current repair cost estimates were in the region of £7m, but the final overall cost for the project is still not known and would also be subject to inflation.
It said the plan to have one part of the new building occupied by March 2027 and the neonatal unit handed over by November 2027 depended on the success of the repair programme.
The Department of Health said it and the Belfast Trust "are reviewing the factors that have led to cost increases and delays".
A DoH statement said the department was "acutely aware of the pressures on public finances".
Adding: "Should specific liability be established, we will ensure that the relevant parties are held accountable."
Building handed over 'in accordance with its contractual obligations'
In a statement, Graham Construction said GBHP successfully handed over the hospital to the trust "in accordance with its contractual obligations".
"Prior to handover, all water quality samples tested within the facility were confirmed to be free from pseudomonas aeruginosa (PsA). These tests were independently witnessed and verified by up to seven separate parties providing robust assurance of compliance at the point of handover," said Graham Construction.
"Following completion of the handover process, GBHP has had no involvement in the management, operation, or maintenance of the hospital. GBHP has not been party to, nor involved in, any matters arising after handover, including the ongoing issues relating to water quality within the building."
Delays to mental health facility
The £33m Acute Mental Health facility, on the site of Belfast City Hospital, was opened in 2019 but has also been beset by problems which have forced patients to be relocated.
The repair bill for the facility is £6m, however a further £3.4m has been spent making wards on the Knockbracken Healthcare site in south Belfast suitable to rehouse patients.
Patients are not expected to return to the Acute Mental Health facility until February 2029.

media.alt: A hospital building with two blue fences in front of it. There is a grey sky above.

summary: The maternity building on the Royal Victoria Hospital site is already tens of millions of pounds over budget.

title: 'Such terrible waste' as health trust buildings could cost an extra £20m

Can or not? 2 migrant workers in Singapore using recycling machine sparks debate
A video of the two workers using the machine to get a refund for their empty drink cans prompted their employer to issue a clarification
The refund is small – 10 Singapore cents (8 US cents) per bottle – for each return under Singapore’s Beverage Container Return Scheme (BCRS). But the uproar is big.
Since BCRS reverse vending machines became fully operational on October 1, Singapore’s social media has been flooded with videos and posts criticising people for raiding bins and holding up others by returning containers by the bag-load.
A recent controversy was sparked by a post on October 28 showing two town council workers returning empty drink cans at a BCRS machine.

content:
（ 德国之声中文网）在11月4日中国外交部的例行记者会上，针对中美俄方面正安排三国元首在深圳APEC会议期间举行会议的报道，中国外交部发言人毛宁回应道：“中方就中俄美元首会晤同相关方保持着沟通。”
莫斯科方面的表态看起来更加确定。据德新社报道，克里姆林宫发言人佩斯科夫（Dmitri Peskow）周二在记者会上表示，“理论上来讲”，各方都愿意举行这次会晤，“三方都认为举行会谈是件好事”。 普京 的外交政策顾问乌沙科夫也表示：“我们的中国朋友——APEC峰会的东道主，会处理好此事，更确切地说，他们已经在筹备这次会谈了。”
不过，无论是中国外交部发言人毛宁、还是克里姆林宫方面，都没有具体阐述这场可能的会谈将聚焦哪些议题。特朗普在10月中旬表示，他们可以讨论核武器、无核化和贸易等问题。
会晤是否会聚焦乌克兰问题？
上周结束对华访问后，德国总统施泰因迈尔接受了德国电视一台（ARD）采访，披露了与 中国领导人习近平 会晤的细节。当时，德国电视一台记者戴斯（Matthias Deiß）提问：“最近有消息称，中国希望或将与美国和俄罗斯进行共同谈判，可能还会涉及 乌克兰问题 。对此，您能向我们透露些什么？”
施泰因迈尔回答说：“我读到这类报道，也直接向习近平主席提及此事。从他的面部表情可以看出，他似乎有些困惑，因为他随后反问，这些传闻从何而来。”
德国总统施泰因迈尔：听闻“三方峰会” 习近平面露困惑
这位德国总统表示，习近平提到了即将在中国深圳举行的亚太经合组织（APEC）峰会，但认为目前根本没有筹备任何由美国、俄罗斯和中国三方参与的乌克兰问题峰会。
不对等的伙伴关系？俄罗斯日益依赖中国

施泰因迈尔补充道，习近平对此还明确表示：“这是一个欧洲的冲突，欧洲人必须坐到谈判桌前。”
普京最渴望这次会晤？
乌克兰总统泽连斯基曾在10月警告，担心此次三方峰会成为一个新版的“雅尔塔会议”（1945年的雅尔塔会议确立了二战后的国际秩序和影响力分配）。 “我们确实不希望这演变成‘雅尔塔2.0、3.0、4.0’，导致影响力的重新分配，”他说道。
泽连斯基也表示：“俄罗斯比任何人都更渴望这次会晤。”他警告称，不应让莫斯科获得“又一个重大的外交优势”。

The curbs have intensified calls for India to develop its own advanced tunnelling equipment and boost its manufacturing sector
Experts say while the curbs are unlikely to halt construction, they could slow major projects and have intensified calls for India to develop its own advanced tunnelling equipment.
The restrictions also threaten to complicate a cautious thaw in relations between the Asian neighbours, raising questions about how far their economic ties can recover amid persistent strategic tensions.
India’s Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said on Tuesday that Delhi would not bow to pressure or make concessions to secure critical technology from China, but would instead develop its own manufacturing capabilities if supplies were restricted.
